newsitem.title: USA: Bay State says '98 EPS estimates too low.
newsitem.headline: Bay State says '98 EPS estimates too low.

text.p: Bay State Gas Co reported said Tuesday that given the early effects of 1996's restructuring and cost management efforts, current analyst consensus estimates appear low for the next two years.
The company said estimates for fiscal 1997 are $1.94 to $2.04 per share, but that it expects weather-adjusted earnings will be towards the upper half of this range.

The company also said it expects to exceed estimates of between $2.08 and $2.13 per share for fiscal 1998, given the continued improvement in its utility business and modest contributions from EnergyUSA its nonregulated subsidiary.

Bay State said that it expects to invest between $1 million and $2 million in capital (excluding acquisitions) in 1997 in Energy USA, and to incur operating losses of $0.07 to $0.12 per share on revenues of $40-50 million as it proceeds to expand that business.

By 1998 however, the company said it expects to invest between $5 million and $10 million in capital (excluding acquisitions) and to achieve an earnings contribution of $0.07 to $0.12 per share on revenues of $80-100 million.

Bay State said its growth strategies include a combination of grassroots expansions, alliances, and continued mergers and acquisitions. It said capital to support the growth will come from a variety of sources, including divestiture of non-strategic assets, new stock issuances and alliances.
